forward to the nearest microphone, clearly state their name and address when recognized and

Manchester School District Sees Academic Gains in 2026 State Assessment 
Results 
MANCHESTER, N.H.- The Manchester School District is seeing encouraging 
improvement in its 2026 New Hampshire Student Assessment System (NHSAS) results, 
with districtwide proficiency increasing in reading and writing, mathematics, and 
science. 
From 2025 to 2026, districtwide proficiency increased from 28% to 31% in reading and 
writing, 18% to 20% in mathematics, and 14% to 17% in science. 
While we know there is still significant work ahead of us, we are encouraged by the 
gains we are seeing across the District, particularly in several of our elementary grades. 
Some of our strongest gains can be seen in elementary literacy. Third-grade reading 
and writing proficiency increased from 25% to 32% (7% increase), fourth grade 
increased from 30% to 34% (4% increase), and fifth grade increased from 24% to 32% 
(8% increase). 
We are also seeing positive movement in mathematics. Third-grade mathematics 
proficiency increased from 26% to 32% (6% increase), while fourth grade increased 
from 28% to 30%. Districtwide mathematics proficiency increased two percentage 
points overall. 
Science also showed improvement, with districtwide proficiency increasing from 14% to 
17%. Fifth-grade science increased from 12% to 17%. 
These results are encouraging, but they represent just one measure of student learning 
in our continued work to improve outcomes for Manchester students. State assessment

The goals as discussed on August 31st are below.

and implementation of the district dashboard will be an important action step, along with 
strengthened engagement between Board members, schools, and city partners. 
Timeline for Dashboard was discussed.   
 The Board Clerk will distribute a survey to Board members requesting feedback 
regarding the information and metrics they would like included on the dashboard. 
 Board members will identify desired dashboard data and metrics. 
 Administration will review the requests and determine what data can reasonably be 
provided. 
 A draft is anticipated for review in approximately November. 
 The goal is to have a more finalized dashboard available by the January Board retreat. 
 
2. Board Development and Training:  The Board will strengthen its effectiveness through 
professional development, including contract-negotiation training to happen this fall with 
District Attorney Matt Upton and a Board development retreat with the superintendent in 
January. The retreat will focus on Board governance, Board operations, the Board/ 
superintendent relationship, and opportunities to improve the Board’s effectiveness. 
 
 
3. Strategic Plan Update:  The Board will begin updating the district strategic plan through 
the creation of an ad hoc committee. The committee will review the existing plan, assess 
progress, identify areas requiring updates, determine the appropriate process for 
community participation, and make recommendations to the full Board. 
 
The Board Clerk will contact all Board members, including those not in attendance, to 
determine who is interested in serving on the ad hoc committee. The membership of the 
committee will then be announced at a subsequent full Board meeting.
